> I leave a local server running my backend projects 24/7, and I want a physical dashboard to monitor its physical environment. I'll use a Raspberry Pi 4, a DHT22 sensor, and some LEDs inside a custom case. The Pi will run a web server so I can check the stats, and the LEDs will alert me if the area around the hardware gets too warm.

## Design

### 2026-10-01 — Spent this session researching the components, planning the stack, and getting the 3D design done.

**6.5h**

Spent this session researching the components, planning the stack, and getting the 3D design done.

I started with some research into the hardware requirements to pick the right parts for the job. Instead of a basic microcontroller, I went with a Raspberry Pi 4 so I can run Node.js

 and a local SQLite database to log temperature trends over time. I mapped out the wiring for the DHT22 sensor and warning LED (including the 330Ω resistor), planned the architecture, and wrote the documentation in the README.

After that, I modeled the custom enclosure in Onshape. Knowing the Pi 4 runs warm, I designed ventilation slots and isolated the DHT22 mount so the board heat will not mess with ambient readings. Finally, I exported the STLs, organized the repository into clean /images and /stl folders, and synced everything up.
